basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models the movement, shipment and consignment, while the goods, vehicles and handling units are mastered elsewhere.
Status is derived from observations and custody assertions, not set by hand.
Covers multimodal legs and replanning with ETA, unlike a single transport booking.
Separate from the sale and title transfer of the goods it moves.

may: Record movement events with time, place and source.
Compute and publish ETAs with stated confidence.
Report exceptions such as delay, damage or temperature excursion.
Propose replanned routes to the responsible planner.
mustNot: Declare goods to customs or sign transport documents on anyone's behalf.
Release goods to a party without verified custody handover.
Hide or smooth over condition excursions for sensitive cargo.
Misdeclare dangerous goods or skip their handling rules.
Share shipment locations of high-value cargo with unauthorized parties.
requiresHuman: Accepting or rejecting damaged or excursion-affected cargo.
Changing the consignee or delivery address after dispatch.

considerations: Dangerous goods and cold-chain failures can harm people far from the shipment.
Driver and courier tracking data is personal data and can be used for intrusive monitoring.
Transport emissions should be measured and reported honestly.

items: Gross mass in kilograms including packaging, measured at handover.
Volume in cubic metres and outer dimensions in metres of each handling unit.
Temperature in degrees Celsius during transit, with logger position and interval.
Relative humidity in percent during transit, where cargo is sensitive.
Shock or acceleration in g, recorded by a logger on the handling unit.
Position as latitude and longitude in WGS 84 with timestamp.
A consignment is recognised by its shipment identifier on labels and documents, its handling units and its seal numbers.
It is confused with the order it fulfils, the vehicle that carries it and other consignments in the same container.
Loss, theft or misdelivery of goods.
Injury from badly secured or overweight loads.
UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods.
WCO Data Model for customs declarations.
